about: The English of 1750: every word the web app puts on screen, in the manner of Samuel Johnson's Preface to the Dictionary as first printed in 1755. A shadow of copy/en.json, which holds the schema (surface, apps, example); a key missing here falls back to it. Spelling as copy/en-x-1750.spelling.json; no stage-play archaisms, no capitalised common nouns, and the long s only in app.titlePage. Design: LANGUAGE.md section 6.

readout.sub.coldAssumes.text: about {boil} to boil, as experience has shewn

readout.sub.coldAssumes.more.text: As often as you tap It boils in earnest, having begun from cold water, I note how long the water was in coming to the boil, and mix that equally with what I had before for the same quantity. Your pots I cannot tell apart; I know only how much water is in them. Where I have never timed so much, I reckon from the nearest quantity I have. Tap the boil to-day, and I shall correct the time while the eggs are cooking.

refusal.whiteNeverSets.text: With the heat withdrawn, the water cools before the white is set, and no setting can succeed. Add more water, or keep it boiling.

refusal.harderThanPan.text: With the heat withdrawn, this quantity of water ({water}) grows cool before the yolk arrives there. Firmest attainable: {limit}. Add more water, or keep it boiling.

refusal.counter.text: An egg left upon the table does not cease to cook because it has ceased to boil. Softest attainable: {limit}. In iced water it might be left softer.

refusal.tap.text: A cold tap cools the egg too slowly to arrest the yolk. Softest attainable: {limit}. In iced water it might be left a little softer.

refusal.unlikelySoft.text: The softest in which I hitherto succeed at least {hits} times in {of}: {limit}.

refusal.unlikelyHard.text: The firmest in which I hitherto succeed at least {hits} times in {of}: {limit}.

refusal.ice.text: Any shorter, and the white is yet raw. Softest attainable for this egg: {limit}.

action.hint.heating.more.text: A full boil is not the first bubbles at the edge, but the whole surface heaving, and not to be calmed by stirring. The rest of the cook is timed from your tap, which teaches me likewise how fast your stove brings water to the boil; a few seconds either way are of no moment, but a minute early is an errour. Until you tap, the countdown is but my conjecture.

controls.egg.more.text: The heat must reach the middle of the egg, and the middle of a bigger egg lies further from the water. A size printed upon the box comprehends eggs of very different weights; if therefore you have scales, weigh one and enter its weight, and I shall trust the scales before the box.

controls.measure.legend.text: Or measure it; any one suffices

controls.measure.hint.text: Scales are the most exact. Otherwise wrap a slip of paper round the fattest part, and measure the slip, which is easier than to caliper an egg. The other two boxes follow from whichever you fill.

controls.eggFrom.more.text: A fridge keeps its eggs at much the same warmth from day to day, so that I know where a fridge egg begins. A room may be some degrees warmer or cooler than I suppose, and every degree moves the time a little; if you know better, choose Your own, and tell me. An egg that has stood out is as warm as the room, and therefore tells me likewise the warmth of your kitchen, which signifies when the eggs rest upon the table, or the fire is put out.

controls.eggFrom.hint.text: Supposed temperatures: fridge, {fridge}; room, {room}. Choose Your own if yours differ.

controls.start.more.text: Boiling water: lower the eggs into water already at a full boil, and the clock begins as they go in; they peel more easily. Cold water: the eggs in a cold pan, the fire lit, and you tap when it boils, which teaches me how fast your stove boils water; they are done sooner, the waiting for the boil included. Sous-vide: I shall tell you when you ought to have begun, which is commonly some while ago.

controls.afterTheBoil.more.text: Keep it boiling: the fire holds the water at a full boil till the eggs come out, and the quantity of water is of little moment. Fire out, lid on: the eggs once in boiling water, put out the fire and put on the lid, and the hot water finishes the eggs as it cools. This spares fewel; but the water does all the labour, so that its quantity decides the time, and too little cannot finish the work. If you choose this, measure it.

controls.cooling.more.text: When the eggs come out, the heat in the white continues its progress inward, and the yolk cooks on for some minutes. Iced water carries the heat away fastest, and therefore arrests it soonest, and permits me to offer the softest yolks; a cold tap is nearly as good. Still air takes away scarcely any heat: to a hot egg upon the table it is less a means of cooling than a lid. For this I make allowance; but it forbids the softest yolks, and how much more the yolk will cook is not easily foretold.

controls.water.more.text: The quantity of water in the pan, the eggs not reckoned. It signifies most with the fire out, when the water's own heat does the cooking: more water holds its heat longer. It signifies a little with the fire lit, because cold eggs entering boiling water cool a little water more than a great deal. And I remember how long each quantity you use takes to boil; it is therefore worth measuring.

controls.eggsInPan.more.text: How many eggs go in together. Cold eggs take heat from boiling water as they enter, and more eggs take more; so the water is longer in recovering, or, with the fire out, never recovers. For eggs begun in cold water it makes no difference to my computation: you tap when the water boils, and that already reckons them.

controls.altitude.more.text: The higher you are, the less the air presses down, and the cooler water boils; and cooler water cooks more slowly. The difference accumulates: a kitchen upon a mountain needs sensibly longer than one by the sea. Tell me nearly how high you are, and I shall cook at the boiling point here shewn.

help.how.p1.text: I do not proceed by rule of thumb, which is only the experience of others imperfectly remembered. I compute how heat passes from the water into your egg, and how far the yolk and the white are set in its passage; and then I choose the time that leaves the yolk where you desired it.

help.how.aside.text: In the language of the learned: [heat conduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation) through a sphere of the bigness of your egg, and the setting of white and yolk as a dose of heat accumulated over time, by the [Arrhenius equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrhenius_equation). Every constant, with its authority, is in the [README](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#2-the-physical-model).

help.how.p2.text: The cooling is likewise to be counted. An egg taken from the water continues some minutes to cook from within; iced water stops it soonest, and the table scarcely retards it. To leave the fire is not to leave the heat.

help.how.aside2.text: Upon the table, still air draws off heat so slowly, that the yolk ends within a fraction of a degree of where it would, had the egg never cooled at all. [README §5](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#5-carryover-the-cooling-step-is-part-of-the-recipe).

help.learn.p1.text: Your answers teach me three things: how you like your yolk, how the whites of your eggs behave, and how fast your stove boils water. A reading of the probe teaches me at a stroke how fast heat enters your eggs. No question is compulsory; but every answer is instruction.

help.learn.aside.text: I keep a cloud of conjectures about your eggs and your taste, and every answer alters their weight: [sequential Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particle_filter), with an [ordered probit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordered_probit) for too rear, as was desired, or too hard. I keep every egg; so that when I am improved, I learn again from all of them. [The design](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer/blob/main/INFERENCE.md).

help.reliable.title.text: Of eggs to be relied upon

help.reliable.intro.text: The greatest help is to tell me how each egg came out; after that, all depends upon your manner of cooking.

help.reliable.forYou.text: For the eggs as now set out

help.reliable.every.text: Weigh the egg if you can: one size upon the box comprehends eggs that need very different times. Eggs straight from the fridge are more certain than eggs at the warmth of the room.

help.reliable.hot.text: Of all methods the easiest to perform rightly. Keep the water at a full boil the whole time.

help.reliable.cold.text: Tap It boils in earnest when the whole surface rolls, not at the first bubbles. That tap corrects my time while the eggs are cooking.

help.reliable.heatOff.text: The water does all the cooking; measure it therefore, and be liberal. With too little, the white will never set.

help.reliable.cooling.text: Iced water is the most certain, a cold tap nearly as good, and the table suffers the yolk to cook on. For soft eggs, use ice.

help.odds.p1.text: Under the time, I say which way an egg is likely to miss. The bracket under the slider shews where the yolk will probably fall. When a miss is likely enough to signify, I propose a degree that plays safe, one tap away, and never one where the white may be unset. All of it grows narrower as I learn; for knowledge is, in great part, only errour diminished.

help.odds.aside.text: The bracket comprehends eight eggs in ten. When I choose the time, a white left unset is reckoned three times worse than a yolk a little too firm; I therefore incline somewhat to the longer side. I propose to play safe when either way of missing is at least one egg in five: firmer means nine yolks in ten at least as firm as you asked, and softer the reverse of that, with the danger to the white under one in five. The shading of the slider shews how often each degree comes out right for you.

help.unsure.counter.text: The table. No one appears to have made publick how fast an egg cools in still air, and that is therefore the weakest of my numbers.

help.unsure.heatOff.text: The fire out. I suppose an ordinary pan with its lid on; a heavy pot or a loose lid will alter the time.

help.unsure.white.text: Whites. I cannot distinguish a white that sets late from a cook who calls a tender white unset.

help.unsure.sousVide.text: Sous-vide. Below {floor} the white remains liquid and moves within the shell, which I leave out of my account; there I am not to be trusted. The very long times are real, however: so cool, the white takes the better part of a day to set.

help.sources.intro.text: The chief authorities behind my numbers. The [README](https://github.com/danmackinlay/actual_egg_timer#10-references) lists them all, with what each has settled.

help.source.williams.text: C. D. H. Williams, "The Science of Boiling an Egg", University of Exeter (1998). newton.ex.ac.uk/teaching/CDHW/egg (the host is gone; the page is in the Internet Archive)

help.source.buay.text: D. Buay, S. K. Foong, D. Kiang, L. Kuppan and V. H. Liew, "How long does it take to boil an egg? Revisited", European Journal of Physics 27, 119-131 (2006). doi:10.1088/0143-0807/27/1/013

help.source.abbasnezhad.text: B. Abbasnezhad, N. Hamdami, J.-Y. Monteau and H. Vatankhah, "Numerical modeling of heat transfer and pasteurizing value during thermal processing of intact egg", Food Science & Nutrition 4, 42-49 (2016). doi:10.1002/fsn3.257

help.source.denys.text: S. Denys, J. G. Pieters and K. Dewettinck, "Computational fluid dynamics analysis of combined conductive and convective heat transfer in model eggs", Journal of Food Engineering 63, 281-290 (2004). doi:10.1016/j.jfoodeng.2003.06.002

help.source.vega.text: C. Vega and R. Mercadé-Prieto, "Culinary Biophysics: on the Nature of the 6X °C Egg", Food Biophysics 6, 152-159 (2011). doi:10.1007/s11483-010-9200-1

help.source.weijers.text: M. Weijers, P. A. Barneveld, M. A. Cohen Stuart and R. W. Visschers, "Heat-induced denaturation and aggregation of ovalbumin at neutral pH described by irreversible first-order kinetics", Protein Science 12, 2693-2703 (2003). doi:10.1110/ps.03242803

idle.welcome.text: This is our first egg together. I begin by reasoning from eggs in general; but as you tell me how each one came out, I learn to reason from yours.

controls.units.more.text: Metrick or imperial, for every number I shew and every number you enter. I begin with what is customary where your browser says you are. To change them alters the manner of writing the numbers, and, from the imperial, the stile of my English; the egg and the times remain exactly the same, and the eggs are indifferent to either.

controls.thermometer.more.text: If you have a probe thermometer, I shall ask for one reading when the counting-down of the cooling ends. That is the moment at which the middle of the yolk is warmest; thrust the point therefore to the very middle, and tell me the highest number you see: anywhere else, or any later, reads lower. From that single egg I learn how fast heat enters your eggs. When the eggs rest upon the table I do not ask, because nothing is counted down.

controls.thermometer.ask.text: Ask a reading after every egg
